answers.reason: The president leads the university and chairs its central bodies, such as the senate which decides on university-wide strategy and structure.
The university leadership sets the budget and the president chairs the central bodies, though the chancellor is primarily responsible for the budget.
Members only sit in the one body that deals with their specific matters, and the president only chairs central strategy bodies.
The faculty council is chaired by the dean to decide faculty affairs, and higher officers do not sit in bodies dealing with other matters.
The president does not sit in bodies that deal with teaching and degree programmes, as every member takes part in only one place.
The president does not sit in bodies dealing with individual student examination matters, regardless of holding a higher office.
This round awards faculty internal grants, which is outside the president's single designated place of participation.
Rewriting module descriptions for a degree programme falls outside the central university matters assigned to the president.
Choosing equipment for a teaching laboratory is a specific matter separate from the president's central leadership role.
Planning the first week for new students is not the central body where the president takes part.
